name: domain-entry-keys
of: A mechanism by which a stranger gains working orientation in an unfamiliar important domain in one move, named with the key, its carrier (a distinction, a unit, a chair, a document, a question, a word, a failure, a habit), one domain where it opens the door, and the domain where the same key opens the wrong door; sorted by how much of the key survives a crossing between domains, from keys that are the same in every lock to keys the domain re-cuts as soon as they are copied.
items: Prey question: in every domain the stranger's first instinct is the outcome question, is it serious, will I win, how much, is this a good buy, and asking it hands the native the frame, since an outcome question is answered by whatever the native decides to say; the key is the question's shape, held so as not to ask it, and the shape is the same in a clinic, a law office, a car lot, and a garage, which is why it is the one key here that needs no re-cutting; it opens the wrong door where the outcome is the domain's whole product, as with a bookmaker, since there the outcome question is the peer question and the withheld one reads as a bluff.

Magic word: an institution keeps an exception path where its real machinery is reachable, and a stranger enters it with a protocol token rather than a reason, in writing, for the record, I'd like the attending to see this, the form number said aloud at the counter; the form of the token travels between domains (ask for a writing, ask for a record, ask for the senior) while the phrase is local; it opens the wrong door where the token is also the marker of trouble, so the patient who asks for the attending is charted as difficult and the litigant who cites the form number is flagged as the kind who reads forms, and the exception path routes to the domain's defenses rather than its machinery.

Switchboard chair: the person whose job is to know who knows sits in a low chair with the whole map, the ward clerk, the court clerk, the department administrator, the crew's fixer, the sysadmin, and the key is the chair rather than the person, since it is nearly the same chair in every institution and can be found from outside; not low-chair-advantages' account of what the chair confers on its occupant, but the stranger's one use of it, a routing; it opens the wrong door in craft and small domains, where the knower is the master and there is no switchboard, and in domains whose front desk is built to deflect, where the chair is a gate and the map is withheld.

Confluence chore: the menial task that sits where every flow of the domain crosses, prep in a kitchen, retracting in surgery, document review in a lawsuit, on-call in a service, obituaries in a newsroom, teaches the domain's traffic in one shift because everything passes through it; the key is the task's position in the flow, not its lowliness, which is what it adds to low-chair-advantages; it opens the wrong door where the chore has been outsourced or automated off the confluence, contract dishwashers, e-discovery, so the stranger who takes it learns the outsourced thing and nothing else.

Native gripe: what natives complain about without expecting change is the negative image of the domain's control surface, since people gripe about what they cannot move, nurses about staffing, academics about grant cycles, farmers about weather and the price, pilots about the roster, so an hour in the break room lists the binding constraints; the reading rule travels, the list does not; it opens the wrong door where the gripe is ritual, a bonding complaint whose object nobody would change, as with an orchestra and its conductor, and where the true constraint is a person in the room and therefore never said.

Native period: every domain has a period inside which things can happen and outside which nothing moves, the court term, the fiscal quarter, the growing season, the academic year, the sprint, the liturgical year, and the stranger who learns it learns when to ask and when asking is noise; not the time a thing takes but the window in which it can be asked for at all, and not a clock read off a state but a calendar natives assume; it opens the wrong door where the visible calendar hides the operative one, the academic year seen and the grant cycle running, or where the domain performs continuity, markets and newsrooms, while running on a hidden period, the close and the deadline.

Stop-holder: every domain has a person or office whose no ends the matter regardless of rank, the pharmacist who will not fill, the building inspector, the completion-bond company on a film, the clerk who will not docket, the anaesthetist who will not put the patient under, and the key is to find the no rather than the yes, since a yes above a no is a wish; the slot travels, the office must be re-found; it opens the wrong door where the formal stop is not the real one, a board whose veto is ceremonial over a founder's mood, and in consensus cultures where the no is distributed and no one holds it, so the stranger who finds the stop-holder finds a chair with nobody in it.

Native unit: the unit natives count in compresses what the domain is short of, beds and patient-days, matters and billable hours, covers, acres and head, containers, seat-miles, person-years, points and picas, so learning the unit tells the stranger what the domain pays for before anyone explains it; not the unit that is priced, which pricing-unit-metamorphoses follows, but the unit said in the corridor; it opens the wrong door where the unit is a badge rather than a measure, kept from a time when it tracked the scarcity, the billable hour where the sale is now the outcome, the film crew's day where the cost is the setup, so the stranger reads a scarcity that is dead, a ghost-leverage worn as a count.

Native tolerance: the same unit at a different precision marks the domain, the bookkeeper to the cent and the CFO to the million, the framer to the eighth, the machinist to the thousandth, the surveyor to a millimetre over a kilometre, and a stranger who reports at the wrong precision is identified in one sentence, while the native tolerance tells what the domain can actually control; not what is counted but how finely, so two natives of one unit can be strangers to each other; it opens the wrong door where the stated tolerance is aspiration, a spec sheet the shop floor does not meet, or where precision is theatre, a forecast to three decimals, so the stranger matches a precision nobody works at.

Fatal class: every domain sorts its errors into a small class that cannot be undone and a large class that can, the missed filing deadline, the wrong-side operation, the jibe in a following sea, the dropped table, and a stranger can act at all only once they hold the short list, because slowness buys something only against the fatal class and native speed elsewhere looks reckless until the list is known; not the domain's famous failure but the shape of its error space; it opens the wrong door where the fatal class is unmarked because the domain is young enough that natives have not met it, or where the list is kept deliberately vague to keep juniors slow everywhere.

Founding wreck: a domain's rules are fossils of its failures, and the failure everyone can name, the bridge that galloped, the wrong-patient transfusion, the fund solvent on paper and dead on cash, is the key to which rules are load-bearing, since a rule with a wreck behind it is broken at one's peril and a rule without one is a habit; not the fatal class, since a wreck can stand behind a rule that guards a recoverable error; it opens the wrong door where the famous wreck is the domain's legend, a business-school case, and the shaping failures are hidden, classified, settled under seal, or filtered by survival, so the stranger reads the failure the domain wants seen.

Hinge distinction: the cut natives make before anything else, acute or chronic, civil or criminal, standing or none, income or capital, static or dynamic load, authentication or authorization, reorganizes the domain's whole pile around one binary, and a stranger who holds it can follow any native conversation because every sentence assumes it; not hinge-kinds' latent variable that decides between two advices, but the cut made before advice exists; it opens the wrong door when the stranger carries the last domain's hinge, the physician asking a lawyer whether the matter is acute and hearing time-barred, and where a domain's first cut is social, who is asking, so the technical hinge opens onto a room where nothing happens.

False friend list: the words a stranger already owns that reverse inside the domain are a short list that does most of the damage, positive in medicine, conservative in surgery, consideration in contract, sanction in law, theory in science, aggressive in oncology against aggressive in finance, and the key is that the list is short and each reversal total, so a stranger carrying the outside meaning is fluent and wrong in the same sentence; the carried word is the general failure of every key on this map caught at the size of one word; it opens the wrong door where the danger is an orphan rather than a false friend, a native term with no outside referent, a tort, a p-value, which the list cannot catch because there is nothing to reverse.

Read sheet: the document everyone in the domain actually reads is the one that binds today's action, the judge's standing order and not the code, the handoff sheet and not the textbook, the on-call rota and not the org chart, the drawing's revision log, the prep list, the docket, the build config, and the key is that the read document is the domain's working interface while the taught document is its legitimation; no slot travels, since which document is read is an accident of each domain's day; it opens the wrong door where the read sheet is oral and lives in the foreman's head, or where the domain keeps a public playbook as a decoy and the sheet it reads is the one it would never hand a stranger.

Tourist key: a domain that must face many strangers manufactures a stranger-facing simplification that is stable, teachable, and false, the patient leaflet, the introductory course, the public standards page, the price list, and the stranger who learns it becomes fluent at the wrong level, since natives never say it and the tell that catches them is their fluency in it; observed as far as the unsaid simplification, speculative in the clause that natives make it because they cannot name their own keys; it opens the wrong door wherever it is offered, which is its point, and the right door only where no natives remain, a dead language, a defunct exchange's rulebook, and the tourist key is all that is left.

Peer question: the question that asks for a value inside the domain's decision structure, what is the differential, what is the standard of review, what is the cap rate, is it the alternator or the battery, shows that the asker holds the structure and lacks only the number, and is answered as a peer is answered; it must be re-found in every domain and is heard only if it is right, since a near miss is the prey question in costume; it opens the wrong door in that a peer is not taught, because instruction flows to declared novices, and in a competitive domain the peer answer is a competitor's answer, so the stranger who passes buys speed at the price of the domain's teaching.

Kept tell: the expert's tell that separates the real thing from its imitation is a cost the imitator will not pay or a habit the imitator cannot know to fake, the surgeon watching hands rather than words, the contractor who asks about drainage first, the engineer who reads the error path before the happy path, the sommelier who spits, and the key is to learn the tell before the vocabulary, since vocabulary is what the imitation has; it is the one key the domain re-cuts when copied; it opens the wrong door where the tell has leaked and been priced, the confidence man's textbook, the trained interviewee, the counterfeit with the right stitching, so the imitation carries the tell, natives move to a new one, and the stranger holds last year's key.

source.register: Concrete and institutional: ward clerks, standing orders, billable hours, wristbands, prep lists, patient leaflets, false-friend words, the galloping bridge; drawn from medicine, law, kitchens, construction, aviation, sailing, film sets, farming, software, and publishing.
source.mode: Analytical distinctions with observed illustrative cases, each simplified to one mechanism; one item (Tourist key) carries a marked speculative clause about why natives manufacture the decoy, and Native gripe's reading rule is analytical rather than observed.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not an empirical taxonomy or a partition; a real entry into a domain uses several keys at once, and the list makes no claim to cover every kind.
The seriation is an itinerary of how much of a key survives a crossing between domains, not a ranking of value, difficulty, or order of use; map edges are conditional authored claims.

The illustrative cases (ward clerks, standing orders, the galloping bridge, e-discovery, patient leaflets, the billable hour) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about particular institutions or histories.

Tourist key's clause that natives manufacture the decoy because they cannot name their own keys is speculative and marked as such; the item stands on the observed part, a stable, teachable, unsaid simplification.
Study methods, mentors, credentials, and the domain's own gates are outside: a key here is what a stranger can hold in one move, not a course of study or a status the domain confers.

seriation.axis: How much of the key survives the crossing between domains: from keys that are the same in every lock (the outcome question one must not ask), through keys whose form travels while the phrase, person, or task is local, to keys whose slot travels but whose value must be re-cut (period, stop, unit, tolerance, fatal list, wreck, hinge), to a key with no stable slot (the read sheet), to keys the domain cuts for you falsely (the tourist key), keys that must be found against the domain and are heard only if right (the peer question), and finally the key the domain re-cuts as soon as it is copied (the kept tell).
seriation.note: An authored walk, not a scale of value or a sequence of use. Prey question opens because it is the one key identical in every lock: the outcome question is the same everywhere and the key is not to ask it. Kept tell closes because it is the one key the lock re-cuts as soon as it has been copied. Hinge distinction → False friend list is the hinge of the route: the hinge is the value that must be re-cut, and the false friend is what a carried value does, the same word with its load reversed, so the adjacency teaches that the failure clause of every item on this map is one mechanism, a value carried across a slot; this is what the live question about which keys transfer turned into, since what transfers is the slot and the transfer of a value is the wrong door. Read sheet follows as the first key with no slot at all, then the three keys that involve the domain's own hand: Tourist key, which it cuts for you falsely, Peer question, which must be found against it, and Kept tell, which it withholds.

exploration.first_question: By what mechanisms does a stranger gain working competence in an unfamiliar important domain fast, and which of those keys transfer between domains while which must be re-found every time?
exploration.changed_question: Which keys does the domain hand to strangers and which must be taken against it, and what does a handed key do to the one who holds it? Breath one treated every key as something a stranger picks up from a domain indifferent to being entered; sharpening Read sheet against the patient leaflet showed that domains hand strangers keys, that the handed key is stable, teachable, and unsaid by natives, and that the tell which catches the holder is fluency in it. A second change came from writing the failure clause of each item: the same mechanism appeared every time, a value carried across a slot, which turned the transfer question into the seriation axis.

priorities.item: Switchboard chair: the person whose job is to know who knows sits in a low chair with the whole map, the ward clerk, the court clerk, the department administrator, the crew's fixer, the sysadmin, and the key is the chair rather than the person, since it is nearly the same chair in every institution and can be found from outside; not low-chair-advantages' account of what the chair confers on its occupant, but the stranger's one use of it, a routing; it opens the wrong door in craft and small domains, where the knower is the master and there is no switchboard, and in domains whose front desk is built to deflect, where the chair is a gate and the map is withheld.
priorities.why: It is the cheapest key to test from outside and the edge that hangs on it (the routing question is the hinge said aloud) would, if it holds, make the hardest key on the map reachable through the easiest one.
priorities.next_question: Call the main line of three institutions you do not know (a county court, a hospital, a university department), ask only who would know who handles a stated problem, and write down the question each chair asks before routing; check whether that question is the domain's hinge distinction. If it is in two of three, the edge holds; if the chairs route without asking, the edge is cut.

priorities.item: Tourist key: a domain that must face many strangers manufactures a stranger-facing simplification that is stable, teachable, and false, the patient leaflet, the introductory course, the public standards page, the price list, and the stranger who learns it becomes fluent at the wrong level, since natives never say it and the tell that catches them is their fluency in it; observed as far as the unsaid simplification, speculative in the clause that natives make it because they cannot name their own keys; it opens the wrong door wherever it is offered, which is its point, and the right door only where no natives remain, a dead language, a defunct exchange's rulebook, and the tourist key is all that is left.
priorities.why: Low plausibility that the speculative clause survives, since natives may withhold their keys on purpose rather than by incapacity, but high generative promise: it asks whether every institution that faces strangers must build a false surface, and whether the surface can be dated by which tell it lacks.
priorities.next_question: Take one domain's stranger-facing document (a patient leaflet, an introductory syllabus) and one week of native talk (a ward round, a lab meeting); count how many of the leaflet's distinctions natives ever utter. If the count is near zero, the leaflet is a tourist key; then ask a native to correct it and record whether they can, which separates a decoy kept on purpose from one made by natives who cannot see their own keys.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference

neighbors.left: Fatal class: every domain sorts its errors into a small class that cannot be undone and a large class that can, the missed filing deadline, the wrong-side operation, the jibe in a following sea, the dropped table, and a stranger can act at all only once they hold the short list, because slowness buys something only against the fatal class and native speed elsewhere looks reckless until the list is known; not the domain's famous failure but the shape of its error space; it opens the wrong door where the fatal class is unmarked because the domain is young enough that natives have not met it, or where the list is kept deliberately vague to keep juniors slow everywhere.
neighbors.right: Founding wreck: a domain's rules are fossils of its failures, and the failure everyone can name, the bridge that galloped, the wrong-patient transfusion, the fund solvent on paper and dead on cash, is the key to which rules are load-bearing, since a rule with a wreck behind it is broken at one's peril and a rule without one is a habit; not the fatal class, since a wreck can stand behind a rule that guards a recoverable error; it opens the wrong door where the famous wreck is the domain's legend, a business-school case, and the shaping failures are hidden, classified, settled under seal, or filtered by survival, so the stranger reads the failure the domain wants seen.
neighbors.separating_case: A trading desk's rule against Friday deploys, born from an outage rolled back by Monday: a wreck stands behind the rule, so Founding wreck reads it as load-bearing and the stranger obeys it; but the error was recoverable, so Fatal class says slowness there buys little, and the stranger who reads the fatal list off the rulebook is slow everywhere. The converse separates them again: a young domain with a fatal error nobody has yet met holds a fatal class by reasoning and has no wreck at all.

checks.boundary_case: A mentor, the master who takes you on, is out: tempting because it is the fastest entry there is, but a mentor is a source of keys rather than a key and cannot be held in one move. Switchboard chair is in on exactly that contrast, since a person can be a key when the stranger's one use of them is a routing rather than instruction.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a fork the sequence conceals: Peer question and Confluence chore sit far apart on the itinerary, but the edge between them says the two entrances are incompatible in one person in one room, chosen by the first sentence. It shows a loop the line cannot express, Prey question → Tourist key → Kept tell → Tourist key, where the domain's decoy and the domain's tell chase each other and the stranger who entered by the outcome question circles one level below the natives. It shows two dependencies into Hinge distinction: from Switchboard chair, a passage from a person to a distinction where the routing question is the hinge said aloud, and from False friend list, where a carried word reverses the first cut. And Founding wreck → Fatal class states a conditional the adjacency hides: the wreck is a fair map of the fatal list only when the wreck itself was fatal.
checks.target_preserved: Self-read only; an independent Fable critic in a fresh context is pending. Each admitted item names a thing a stranger can hold in one move and a domain where holding it opens the wrong door; the strange members (a question kept in order not to be asked, a decoy the domain manufactures, a tell the domain re-cuts when copied, a gripe read as the negative of a control surface) are kept as mechanisms rather than softened into advice about learning fast.
